q: Some physical quantities of physics are completely described by a single number (or magnitude) with an appropriate unit. Such quantities are called _____ quantities.
e: Scalar quantities have only magnitude and an appropriate unit.

q: Quantities that have both magnitude and direction are called _____ quantities.
e: Vector quantities require both magnitude and direction for a complete description.

q: In printing, vectors are represented by _____ type, such as $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{E}$, $\mathbf{v}$, $\mathbf{s}$.
e: In printing, vectors are represented by boldface type.

q: In handwriting, vectors are indicated by placing _____ on the top of their symbols.
e: In handwriting, vectors are indicated by placing arrows on the top of their symbols.

q: The magnitude of a vector $\vec{F}$ is written as _____.
e: The magnitude of a vector is a scalar quantity, denoted by absolute value bars.

q: If $\vec{A} = -\vec{B}$, it means $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ are equal in magnitude but have _____ directions.
e: The negative sign indicates that the two vectors have equal magnitude but opposite directions.

q: If $\vec{A} = 2\vec{B}$, the magnitude of $\vec{A}$ is two times the magnitude of $\vec{B}$ and the direction of $\vec{A}$ is _____ that of $\vec{B}$.
e: A positive scalar multiplier means the direction remains the same.

q: If $\vec{A} = -3\vec{B}$, the magnitude of $\vec{A}$ is three times the magnitude of $\vec{B}$ and the direction of $\vec{A}$ is _____ to that of $\vec{B}$.
e: A negative scalar multiplier means the direction is opposite.

q: Using graphical method, the length of the arrow representing a vector is _____ to the magnitude of the vector.
e: Graphically, the arrow's length is drawn proportional to the vector's magnitude.

q: To add $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$, first draw $\vec{A}$. Then draw $\vec{B}$ in such a way that the _____ of $\vec{B}$ is at the tip of $\vec{A}$.
e: Vector addition graphically requires placing the tail of the second vector at the tip of the first.

q: The vector sum $\vec{A} + \vec{B}$ is called the _____ vector.
e: The single vector drawn from the tail of the first to the tip of the second is the resultant vector.

q: Vector addition is _____.
e: Vector addition is commutative, meaning $\vec{A} + \vec{B} = \vec{B} + \vec{A}$.

q: In algebraic notation, vector subtraction is expressed as $\vec{A} - \vec{B} =$ _____.
e: Subtracting a vector is equivalent to adding its negative.

q: Vector subtraction is _____.
e: Vector subtraction is not commutative.

q: The process of sub-dividing a vector into two (or) more vectors is called _____ of a vector.
e: Resolution of a vector is the process of breaking it down into multiple component vectors.

q: The new vectors obtained from the resolution of a vector are called vector _____ of the original vector.
e: The subdivided vectors are referred to as the vector components of the original vector.

q: A useful application of vector resolution is sub-dividing a vector into two perpendicular components, namely, _____ component and _____ component.
e: Vectors are commonly resolved into horizontal and vertical perpendicular components.

q: If $\vec{A}$ is the original vector and $\theta$ is the angle with the x-axis, the x-component is given by _____.
e: The horizontal component adjacent to the angle is calculated using the cosine function.

q: If $\vec{A}$ is the original vector and $\theta$ is the angle with the x-axis, the y-component is given by _____.
e: The vertical component opposite to the angle is calculated using the sine function.

q: Distance travelled by the body is the _____ of the path along which the body moves.
e: Distance is defined as the total length of the actual path taken by the moving body.

q: Displacement is the distance travelled along a _____.
e: Displacement is a vector quantity directed from the starting point to the end point along a particular direction.

q: Distance has no specific direction. It has only magnitude; and therefore, it is a _____.
e: Because distance lacks directional quality, it is classified as a scalar quantity.

q: Displacement has both magnitude and direction; and therefore, it is a _____.
e: Displacement is always directed from the starting point to the end point, making it a vector.

q: The average speed, $v_{av}$, is the ratio of total distance $s$ to _____.
e: Average speed is calculated as the total distance travelled divided by the total time taken.

q: The average velocity, $\vec{v}_{av}$, is the ratio of total displacement $\vec{s}$ to _____.
e: Average velocity is the total displacement divided by the time taken.

q: If the starting point and the end point are the same, the total displacement is zero. Therefore, average velocity is _____.
e: Since average velocity depends on displacement, a zero displacement results in zero average velocity.

q: The speed (or) velocity at a particular instant of time are referred to as _____ speed and _____ velocity.
e: Instantaneous speed and velocity represent the motion at a specific, single instant of time.

q: Instantaneous speed is defined as the limiting value of $\frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t}$ as time $\Delta t$ approaches _____.
e: Instantaneous values are found by taking the limit as the time interval approaches zero.

q: Instantaneous velocity is defined as the time rate of change of _____.
e: Instantaneous velocity is the time rate of change of displacement.

q: Motion with constant velocity is known as _____ motion.
e: Uniform motion occurs when a body moves with constant velocity.

q: If either magnitude (or) direction (or) both magnitude and direction of the velocity changes, the body is said to have an _____.
e: Any change in the magnitude or direction of velocity constitutes acceleration.

q: The average acceleration $a_{av}$ is defined by the equation $a_{av} =$ _____.
e: Average acceleration is the ratio of the change in velocity to the time taken.

q: Instantaneous acceleration is the time rate of change of _____.
e: Instantaneous acceleration is defined as the limiting value of the change in velocity over time.

q: Acceleration is said to be positive if the magnitude of velocity is _____.
e: Positive acceleration corresponds to an increase in the magnitude of velocity over time.

q: Negative acceleration is usually called _____ or retardation.
e: When the magnitude of velocity decreases, the negative acceleration is commonly referred to as deceleration.

q: Motion along a straight line is called _____ motion.
e: Linear motion is the simplest type of motion, occurring along a straight line.

q: In linear motion with constant velocity, the acceleration is _____.
e: Since the velocity is non-varying in constant velocity motion, the acceleration is zero.

q: The equation of motion for a linear motion with constant velocity is $v =$ _____.
e: For constant velocity, the equation relates displacement and time as $v = \frac{s}{t}$.

q: If the rate of change of velocity is constant, the acceleration is said to be _____.
e: A constant rate of change of velocity defines constant acceleration motion.

q: The first equation of motion for constant acceleration is $v =$ _____.
e: The velocity-time relation for constant acceleration is given by $v = v_0 + at$.

q: The equation $v^2 = v_0^2 + 2as$ relates final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration, and _____.
e: This equation is independent of time and directly relates velocity, acceleration, and displacement.

q: The equation for displacement in constant acceleration motion is $s =$ _____.
e: The displacement-time relation for constant acceleration is $s = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2}at^2$.

q: The average velocity $\bar{v}$ in constant acceleration motion is given by $\bar{v} =$ _____.
e: For constant acceleration, the average velocity is the arithmetic mean of the initial and final velocities.

q: In the MKS/SI system, the unit of displacement is _____.
e: The standard SI unit for displacement and distance is the metre.

q: In the CGS system, the unit of velocity is _____.
e: The CGS unit for velocity and speed is centimetre per second.

q: In the FPS system, the unit of acceleration is _____.
e: The FPS unit for acceleration is foot per second square.

q: The unit m s$^{-1}$ is read as _____.
e: The unit m s$^{-1}$ represents metre per second, which is the SI unit of speed or velocity.

q: In a linear motion, the magnitude of the displacement is _____ to the distance moved.
e: In straight-line motion without change of direction, the magnitude of displacement equals the distance moved.

q: As the body is moving with a non-varying velocity, the instantaneous velocity and average velocity are the _____.
e: When velocity is constant, it does not change over time, making instantaneous and average velocities identical.

q: In the equations of motion, we will use positive (+) and negative (-) signs to describe the two _____ directions along a straight line.
e: Since vector notation is omitted in 1D motion equations, positive and negative signs indicate opposite directions.

q: Except Eq. (2.7), the rest equations of motion can be expressed in _____ form.
e: Equations like $v = v_0 + at$ can be written with vector arrows, unlike the scalar-only $v^2 = v_0^2 + 2as$.
The textbook notes that equations (2.7) and (2.8) are mathematically derived from the other three fundamental equations.

q: The instantaneous acceleration $a$ is defined as $a = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} =$ _____.
e: The limiting value of the change in velocity over time is the derivative of velocity with respect to time.

q: A body moving with a constant acceleration of 5 m s$^{-2}$ changes its velocity by _____ in every second.
e: An acceleration of 5 m s$^{-2}$ means the velocity increases or decreases by 5 m s$^{-1}$ each second.

q: The speedometer of a car indicates the _____ speed of the car.
e: A speedometer shows the speed at that particular instant of time, which is the instantaneous speed.

q: When a body is moving along a straight line with a constant speed, the velocity of the body is also constant because its magnitude and direction remain _____.
e: In straight-line motion, constant speed ensures both magnitude and direction of velocity are unchanging.

q: Motion can be described or analyzed conveniently with the help of graphs. The motion graphs are of _____ types.
e: The textbook lists three types of motion graphs: displacement-time, velocity-time, and acceleration-time graphs.

q: The three types of motion graphs are displacement-time graph, velocity-time graph, and _____ graph.
e: The third fundamental motion graph is the acceleration-time graph.

q: The slope of the s-t graph gives the _____.
e: The gradient or slope of a displacement-time graph represents the velocity of the body.

q: The slope of a v-t graph gives the _____ of a body.
e: The rate of change of velocity with respect to time, which is the slope of a v-t graph, equals acceleration.

q: The area under a v-t graph gives the _____ (or) distance moved by the body.
e: Integrating velocity over time yields the total displacement or distance moved.
